title: Camp Upton, segregation, training in Alabama, declining warrant officer
summary: Drafted with Ralph Watkins and separated by race at Camp Upton; trained at Camp Siebert, and turned down a warrant-officer path.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: You didn't say that you and Ralph got called up at the same time and went off at the same time.
Yeah, we went off -- I'm trying to think of this camp. It was Camp Upton.
Camp Upton. That's where we were drafted.
Yeah. So when we got through the line, and they said, 'All the colored here and all the white here,' and that was it. And I didn't see him until --

Yeah. I didn't see him until I got back. Anyway, I did my training in Camp Seibert, Alabama, which there was a little drummer who was at -- he was at another camp in Alabama. Was it Fort Ferguson? Fort McPher -- MacPherson. And he, little Billy, well I think he -- I think he died with Parkinson's Disease. But he was a beautiful cat. He said,
"Kenny, you want to be a warrant officer?" "Because all the warrant officers come by me."
You know? He says, "If you make up your mind you want to be a warrant officer, just put it in your application and I'll pass it."
No, because I didn't want the responsibility.
You know, I said, "Well, I'm a soldier," and as far as I got was T-4, which was a technical sergeant. And I said well, that's enough. You know, I can take responsibility or leave it.
But once I -- I didn't want to become too involved.
